deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource. The default value of DELETE allows unrestricted destructive operations. A generic platform policy can require this to be set to PREVENT, blocking accidental or unauthorized deletion of the sharedflow deployment via terraform destroy or terraform apply. This enforces a deletion-blocking safeguard across all teams without requiring team-specific values, preventing destructive loss of cloud resources at the platform level.

environment.description: The resource ID of the environment.
environment.rationale: This specifies which Apigee environment the sharedflow is deployed to. Environment names are arbitrary, team-specific strings with no platform-enforced security distinction between them. A generic policy cannot constrain this without hardcoding team-specific environment names. The security configuration of the environment itself is governed by the google_apigee_environment resource, not by what is deployed into it.

org_id.description: The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee instance
org_id.rationale: This is a reference to the parent Apigee Organization. The value is inherently team- or project-specific (the organization name). A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific organization identifiers. The security of the organization itself is governed by the google_apigee_organization resource, not by resources that reference it.

revision.description: Revision of the Sharedflow to be deployed.
revision.rationale: This specifies the revision number of the sharedflow to deploy. Revision numbers are sequential, team-specific identifiers. There is no inherently secure or insecure revision number; the security of a revision depends on the sharedflow content within it, which is managed on the google_apigee_sharedflow resource. A generic platform policy cannot determine which revision number is appropriate for any given team or workload.

service_account.description: The service account represents the identity of the deployed proxy, and determines what permissions it has. The format must be {ACCOUNT_ID}@{PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
service_account.rationale: This argument sets the runtime identity of the deployed sharedflow and determines what GCP resources and APIs it can access. Per GCP documentation, the service account represents the identity of the deployed proxy and determines what permissions it has. The format must be {ACCOUNT_ID}@{PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com. When left unset, the deployment operates without a scoped identity, violating the principle of least privilege. The policy enforces both presence (blacklist null/empty) and structural format validation via pattern whitelist (*@*.iam.gserviceaccount.com). The allowed values in the pattern whitelist are organisation-configurable placeholders; the structural pattern itself is the platform-level control, consistent with the kms_key_name pattern used in Artifact Registry policies.

sharedflow_id.description: Id of the Sharedflow to be deployed.
sharedflow_id.rationale: This is a reference to which sharedflow to deploy. It points to another resource whose security (its policies, configuration, and logic) is managed on the google_apigee_sharedflow resource itself. A generic policy cannot determine which sharedflows are safe to deploy without team-specific knowledge of sharedflow names and their contents.
